events.title: DR Congo Ituri: Fighting traps Ebola responders inside hospital and disrupts outbreak response
events.summary: A 23 November UN report says fighting near a hospital in Ituri disrupted Ebola services and forced health and aid teams to shelter in a maternity ward for more than 24 hours.
events.body:
Facts | On 23 November 2026, UN News reported that WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on 22 November that heavy fighting near an Ituri hospital interrupted healthcare and the Ebola response. Medical and aid workers sheltered in a maternity ward for more than 24 hours while WHO sought safe passage. Neither the exact facility nor the combatants were identified in the report. The reported interruption therefore applies to the affected hospital, not every medical facility in Ituri.
Assessment | Ituri faces the simultaneous pressures of armed conflict and a Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak. The operational change is that violence has actually interrupted disease-response capability. Fighting around the facility and loss of safe access provide the best-supported explanation; the available account does not establish deliberate targeting of health workers. Delays in case detection, contact tracing, sample movements, isolation and treatment could accumulate if access remains restricted. For mining, construction and logistics operators, the immediate business exposure is the reliability of emergency care and medically controlled referrals for personnel, including expatriates.
Management actions | Require the medical provider serving each affected project to confirm functioning referral facilities, transport authorizations, travel time and infection-control arrangements. Integrate febrile-illness reporting, on-site isolation and medically supervised transfers into duty-of-care plans. Reauthorize non-essential journeys near the affected facility against specific current security notices. Suspected Ebola cases require health-authority-directed handling rather than improvised relocation.
Indicators | (1) WHO confirmation of the team's safe exit and resumption of hospital services; (2) identification and reopening of access to the affected site; (3) changes in diagnostic turnaround and contact-tracing performance in the health zone; (4) further fighting that restricts other medical facilities. A contained, short disruption would be managed through referrals; repeated disruption across facilities could require lower site occupancy and a revised medevac strategy.
Sources | UN News, 23 November, relaying the WHO chief; Reuters, 22 November. https://www.un.org/en/heavy-fighting-ituri-traps-dr-congo-ebola-responders-who ; https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/who-chief-says-fighting-near-congo-ebola-outbreak-area-disrupts-response-efforts-2026-11-22/

events.title: Libya/Benghazi: Russian Naval Corvette Sunk in Drone-Boat Strike as Ukraine Acknowledges Operation
events.summary: Reuters reported on 23 November that Ukraine said it sank the Russian corvette Mercury at Benghazi naval base using maritime drones. Eastern Libyan authorities also reported a drone-boat attack on a merchant vessel and requested a UN investigation.
events.body:
Facts: Reuters reports dated 22–23 November describe the Russian naval corvette Mercury (also rendered Merkury) capsizing and sinking after a maritime-drone strike at Benghazi naval base. President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Ukraine used seven naval drones and destroyed a Russian Ka-27 helicopter. Eastern Libyan authorities reported ten minor injuries among Russian and Libyan personnel. A Maltese-flagged merchant vessel was separately struck off Benghazi; its crew was rescued. Eastern Libyan authorities requested a UN investigation into the drones' origins and alleged foreign involvement. Russia had not publicly commented at the time. Specific claims about attribution, launch location and battle damage remain attributed to the respective parties.
Assessment: The significant change is the geographic extension of Russia–Ukraine maritime hostilities into North African port waters. Kyiv may be seeking to disrupt Russian Mediterranean logistics and increase the costs of Moscow's African military presence. An alternative explanation is a time-sensitive strike against a particular replenishment opportunity rather than a sustained new Libyan campaign. Eastern Libyan authorities, which maintain security ties with Moscow, now face pressure over port sovereignty, foreign military access and relations with rival western Libyan authorities. The reported merchant-vessel incident extends the immediate exposure beyond naval assets to commercial shipping, port calls, crews and war-risk insurance. There is no reported basis for treating all Benghazi port operations as suspended.
Operational decisions: Operators planning Benghazi port calls, transshipment or offshore personnel movements should obtain current navigation notices, check war-risk cover and diversion costs, and confirm berth windows and crew-security arrangements with carriers. Track four indicators: formal port restrictions; repeat attacks on commercial vessels; follow-on Russian or Ukrainian actions and claims; and any escalation between eastern and western Libyan political actors. Repeated attacks affecting civilian sea lanes would justify revising route risk ratings and schedules.
Sources: https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/zelenskiy-says-ukraine-sank-russian-corvette-near-libyas-coast-hit-cargo-ship-2026-11-23/ ; https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/libyas-eastern-government-suspects-drone-attack-caused-explosion-russian-ship-2026-11-22/

events.title: Niger: Foreign national reportedly abducted, with Niamey or Tillabéri road cited as possible location
events.summary: MDMG Sahel reported on 23 November that a foreign national had been kidnapped on the night of 21 November; the location, nationality and alleged transfer to Mali remain source-level claims.
events.body:
Reported facts | On 23 November 2026, French-language outlet MDMG Sahel reported from multiple contacts that a foreign national was abducted in Niger on the night of Saturday, 21 November. Sources differed over whether it occurred within Niamey or on the Tillabéri–Niamey road. The outlet said early accounts suggested Saudi nationality and a possible transfer to the Ménaka area of Mali. Those are reported leads, not established official findings. No group had claimed responsibility; the outlet associated the incident with Islamic State Sahel, an attribution that remains the outlet's assessment.
Assessment | Niamey concentrates expatriate residences, commercial premises and official missions, while the Tillabéri approach is an important travel exposure. Confirmation of a city kidnapping would point towards the ability to locate, approach and move a foreign target through an urban setting. Confirmation of a road abduction would put the emphasis on predictable journey patterns and exposure on the western approaches. The current reporting supports treating this as a significant foreign-national kidnapping candidate. Criminal facilitation, opportunistic abduction and insurgent-directed kidnapping remain possible operational explanations. Earlier foreign-hostage releases cited by the outlet make coercion and ransom relevant hypotheses, not demonstrated motives in this case.
Management | Distinguish residential and workplace exposure in Niamey from journey exposure on the Tillabéri corridor. Review expatriate night movements, pickup arrangements, driver vetting, accommodation access and disclosure of regular routes. Where travel west of the capital is unavoidable, have the security manager approve specific journeys using verified police and road information. Account for staff through company records rather than assumptions about the reported victim's nationality.
Indicators | (1) Identification and confirmed location from police, diplomatic or family sources; (2) a credible claim or hostage-negotiation development; (3) checkpoint or movement restrictions on the Niamey–Tillabéri corridor; (4) a cluster of comparable incidents involving foreign personnel. The location finding determines whether residential protection or road-journey redesign should receive immediate priority.
Verification | Single specialist local-media account. Original source: https://mdmgsahel.com/niger-nouvel-enlevement-dun-etranger/

events.title: Pakistan Chagai: Driver killed and three injured in cargo-vehicle shooting near Dalbandin
events.summary: A 22 November report citing police says gunmen shot at a Taftan-to-Dalbandin cargo vehicle near Dhadar on the Quetta–Taftan highway, killing the driver and injuring three passengers; another truck was reportedly burned nearby.
events.body:
Reported facts: War Monitor published on 22 November 2026 at 18:41, citing police reports that unidentified gunmen opened fire on a goods vehicle carrying four people from Taftan towards Dalbandin near Dhadar. The driver died and three others were injured. Another truck was reportedly set ablaze in the area, and the outlet says the vehicles lacked security escorts. A 23 November Urdu-language report by The Balochistan Post also describes the fatal Dhadar shooting. Responsibility and motive have not been established.
Assessment: This incident affects the commercial road corridor linking Quetta, Dalbandin and the Taftan border. The combination of gunfire and reported arson creates direct exposure for freight operators, although the evidence does not yet distinguish an organized economic interdiction campaign from localized armed criminality or retaliation. Potential operational transmission includes driver refusals, suspended dispatches, escort and insurance costs, and delayed deliveries. The incident does not establish closure of the entire N40 corridor.
Operational response: Reassess discretionary freight movements through the Dalbandin–Taftan section over the next 48 hours. Obtain the precise incident kilometer point, location of the second burned truck, formal police traffic instructions and escort availability from local transport partners. Preserve dispatch flexibility pending route-specific confirmation. Watch for repeat truck attacks within 72 hours, official restrictions, carrier stoppages and any credible claim of responsibility.
Source: https://warmonitorpk.com/en/news/driver-killed-three-injured-in-chagai-highway-shooting-vehicles-seized-in-separate

events.region: Myanmar / Mong Kung, southern Shan State
events.title: Myanmar Shan State: 25 Chinese nationals detained at alleged scam site in Mong Kung
events.summary: Eleven Media reported on 22 November that security forces detained 25 Chinese men in a 21 November operation near Long San village, Mong Kung, southern Shan State, seizing phones and Starlink terminals.
events.body:
Reported facts | Eleven Media reported on 22 November 2026 that Myanmar security personnel searched an area north of Long San village in Mong Kung Township, southern Shan State, on 21 November after tips from residents. They detained 25 Chinese men at four makeshift shelters and seized two desktop computers, 39 mobile phones, two Starlink terminals and power equipment. According to the outlet's account of initial investigations, the men entered Myanmar through the Yunnan frontier in early November, were promised about RMB6,500 a month, and allegedly used WeChat, Momo and QQ for fake investment propositions, online stores and impersonation scams directed at Chinese victims. These are authorities' allegations as carried by the outlet; detained persons are suspects, not convicted offenders.
Assessment | Another reported crackdown during the same period involved 33 Chinese nationals in Mayangon, Yangon. The Mong Kung event is geographically and operationally distinct and merits a separate event record. Satellite broadband terminals and mobile power at makeshift structures, if the reported inventory is accurate, illustrate how alleged fraud operations can function at sites with limited conventional infrastructure. Such activity would depend on remote recruitment, equipment procurement and digital payment access. A common organizational network linking Shan and Yangon is a hypothesis to test, rather than an established fact.
Business exposure | Companies placing Chinese staff, IT teams and outsourcing contractors in Myanmar or near border corridors should verify employment documents, migration status, contracts, facilities, payments and the lawful use of communications equipment. Examine the sourcing and physical locations of remote subcontractors, particularly where intermediaries obscure end-client identity. Separate partner fraud exposure from legitimate industrial satellite-connectivity use.
Indicators | (1) Charges, consular contact, release or repatriation of the 25 detainees; (2) treatment of devices and associated accounts; (3) documented personnel, financial or equipment links to the Yangon case; (4) additional searches in southern Shan. If a cross-regional coordinated network is established, upgrade supplier vetting across locations; if discrete operations, target controls to actual exposure.
Source | Eleven Media Group, 22 November 2026, reporting attributed investigative claims. https://elevenmyanmar.com/news/25-chinese-nationals-arrested-in-southern-shan-state-over-online-scam-operation?language=en

events.title: Myanmar Yangon: 105 detained in online-scam raid, including 33 Chinese nationals
events.summary: State broadcaster Myanmar International TV reported on 22 November that a 20 November raid in Mayangon resulted in 105 arrests, including 25 Chinese men and eight Chinese women, on suspicion of online financial fraud.
events.body:
Officially reported action | Myanmar International TV reported on 22 November 2026 that a joint security team raided a residential property in Mayangon Township, Yangon, at about 11 p.m. on 20 November. Authorities detained 105 people: 25 Chinese men, eight Chinese women, two Thai women and 70 Myanmar nationals. Computers, telephones and networking devices were seized, with additional equipment found at a nearby address. The broadcaster attributed to preliminary investigators the claim that the group had run online financial scams since around May 2026 and recruited Chinese-speaking workers through Telegram. These are suspects subject to investigation and possible proceedings; the report does not establish individual criminal convictions.
Assessment | The significant development is a large enforcement action involving Chinese nationals in a Yangon urban residential setting, rather than solely at a remote border compound. This expands the practical premises and contractor profiles that compliance teams may need to screen in Myanmar. The report cites a tip-off, which fits a discrete intelligence-led raid. A broader operation against linked international scam networks is another possible explanation but requires evidence connecting different locations and suspects.
Business transmission | Lawful companies using Chinese-speaking personnel or outsourced digital operations in Myanmar should be prepared to document employment status, work authorization, property leases, business activity and ownership of IT equipment. Vet contractors and payment-processing partners against fraud indicators, and ensure that company records distinguish legitimate employees from third-party personnel. Large-scale searches may interrupt a linked property's operations even before courts resolve allegations. Consular access, investigation status and handling of personal or corporate equipment matter to affected individuals and businesses.
Indicators | (1) Filed charges and the number of people actually prosecuted; (2) consular involvement, releases or repatriation of the 33 Chinese nationals; (3) subsequent searches in Mayangon or other Yangon townships; (4) asset-freeze, property-seizure or transaction restrictions. If enforcement expands across unrelated premises, strengthen sector-wide third-party audits; otherwise focus on verified direct relationships with the reported location.
Source | Myanmar International TV, 22 November, citing authorities. https://www.myanmaritv.com/news/online-scam-crackdown-105-people-arrested-online-scam-crackdown-yangon

events.title: Pakistan Chagai: Roadside explosion kills three youths near Khargoshkan southwest of Dalbandin
events.summary: A 21 November Urdu-language report says a motorcycle carrying three teenagers encountered a roadside explosive device near Khargoshkan, killing all three. A Dalbandin hospital official confirmed blast-related deaths.
events.body:
Reported facts: Daily Jasarat reported on 21 November 2026 that seven youths travelling on three motorcycles towards Khargoshkan southwest of Dalbandin encountered an explosive device beside the road. The motorcycle carrying three teenagers was caught in the explosion and all three died. A local hospital executive confirmed blast-related deaths; the victims were reportedly aged 16 to 19. The precise incident date was not separately stated, so the initial report date is used provisionally. The device's origin and placement history remain unknown.
Assessment: The victims were civilian travellers, and the immediate significance is lethal explosive exposure on secondary routes around Dalbandin. Deliberate emplacement, unexploded remnants and other origins remain competing explanations. For commercial operations, the relevant pathways are village liaison travel, motorcycles used by community contacts, remote worksites and unpaved access tracks. This report alone does not establish any closure of the N40 highway. Discovery of further devices would materially change the assessment towards broader route contamination.
Operational response: Obtain the precise Khargoshkan incident location and police examination findings through local security contacts. Avoid discretionary travel on uninspected tracks near the site and prioritize previously checked routes. Record suspicious-object reports from community liaison staff and drivers against exact locations. Follow indicators include police disposal findings, discovery of additional devices, and verified overlap with project travel routes.
Source: https://jasarat.com/2026/11/21/three-youths-killed/

events.title: Oman Khasab: Two tanker projectile-strike reports in the Strait of Hormuz on 21 November
events.summary: UKMTO issued two attack warnings on 21 November: at 0500 UTC an outbound tanker was struck on the stern 11 nautical miles north of Khasab, and at 0550 UTC an engine-room strike was reported 17 nautical miles east. No casualties were reported; whether these were separate ships remains unclear.
events.body:
Facts and attribution: UK Maritime Trade Operations warnings 215-26 and 216-26 record a projectile striking the stern of an outbound tanker 11 nautical miles north of Khasab at 0500 UTC and a separate report of an engine-room strike 17 nautical miles east at 0550 UTC on 21 November. Both advisories report no casualties and undetermined environmental impact. Reuters says it remains unclear whether the reports concern the same vessel. A tanker was also struck and caught fire in the area on 20 November. Neither the responsible actor nor weapon type is established.
Assessment: The concentration of reports around the outbound Musandam passage exposes merchant shipping to direct hull damage and possible loss of propulsion even as vessels leave the strait. Engine-room damage could cascade into towing and rescue requirements, traffic restrictions and war-risk insurance costs. Repeated incidents may cause owners, charterers and insurers to revise assumptions about viable transit windows. Continued military coercion spilling into commercial navigation is a plausible explanation; unrelated maritime weapons incidents remain an alternative. Current advisories do not establish coordination or perpetrator.
Management implications: Energy, chemicals and logistics companies with Hormuz cargoes should verify vessel identity, carrier, cargo, expected transit window and war-risk cover on a voyage-by-voyage basis; obtain updated routing, emergency towing and crew-contact arrangements from ship managers. Procurement teams should quantify inventory and alternate-supply exposure to delayed arrivals. Indicators: UKMTO updates identifying vessels and damage in warnings 215/216, actual strait transit volumes, war-risk premium quotations, and shipping-line or port schedule changes. Verification: two official UKMTO maritime warnings plus Reuters reporting. Sources: https://www.ukmto.org/-/media/ukmto/products/20261121-ukmto_warning_215-26.pdf ; https://www.ukmto.org/-/media/ukmto/products/20261121-ukmto_warning_216-26.pdf ; https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/tanker-hit-by-unknown-projectile-near-omans-khasab-ukmto-says-2026-11-21/

events.region: Sudan / Sennar and Blue Nile states
events.title: Sudan / Sennar: Night curfew and freight restrictions as Blue Nile fighting approaches
events.summary: Sennar authorities imposed a 22:00–04:00 urban curfew and a 20:00–05:00 freight-vehicle restriction on 21 November amid reported armed advances in neighbouring Blue Nile State.
events.body: Facts | Radio Tamazuj reported on 21 November 2026 that Sennar Governor Al-Zubair Hassan Al-Sayed issued Emergency Order No. 6 of 2026, prohibiting movement in towns from 22:00 to 04:00 and goods-vehicle operations across the state from 20:00 to 05:00. Permitted medical and emergency responders are exempt. Local sources separately reported advances by RSF and SPLM-N-aligned forces in Bau and Geissan, including reported control of Taga and Madina 11; residents in Damazin have begun leaving. Territorial claims remain attributed to those local sources. Assessment | The curfew is a pre-emptive attempt to constrain night movement and possible armed infiltration as fighting moves closer to Sennar. An alternative interpretation is that the measure is primarily intended to demonstrate government control before any direct offensive against the state. Business transmission | The order materially reduces the night freight window for fuel, food, medical supplies and project logistics. Mobilisation in East Sennar may also increase checkpoints and inspections. Operators should reschedule cross-state freight to daylight, quantify lost capacity, confirm any permit exemptions and reassess personnel presence and evacuation options toward Damazin. Indicators | (1) Enforcement and exemptions under Order No. 6; (2) independently corroborated control changes in Bau and Geissan; (3) displacement and road access around Damazin; (4) checkpoint delays and freight throughput in Sennar. Source: https://www.radiotamazuj.org/en/news/article/sennar-imposes-night-curfew-as-blue-nile-fighting-intensifies

events.title: Pakistan Chagai: Armed men reportedly seize Los mining site near Nok Kundi and detain personnel
events.summary: A local report dated 19 November says more than 30 armed men seized a mining site near Nok Kundi, detained personnel including a geologist and former security-force members, and damaged equipment.
events.body: Facts: The Balochistan Post reported on 19 November 2026 that more than 30 armed men reportedly entered a mining site in the Los area, detained people including former FC and Sindh Rangers members and a geologist, and damaged machinery. Exact incident time remains to be confirmed; the report date is used provisionally. Assessment: Temporary site seizure and personnel detention threaten contractor safety and operational continuity. Economic coercion against mining and an attack directed at particular individuals are competing explanations. Management: Account for staff and geological teams near Los and Nok Kundi, verify communications and equipment losses, and reauthorize non-essential site visits. Indicators: Detainee release, operator identity, equipment damage, police updates and any claim of responsibility. Verification: single local-media report pending independent confirmation. Source: https://thebalochistanpost.net/2026/11/armed-men-attack-mining-site-in-chagai-and-block-highway-in-khuzdar/

events.title: DR Congo Haut-Uélé: Chinese national and police officer killed in Watsa gold-mine attack
events.summary: Local media reported on 19 November that an armed attack at Ndiyo in Watsa on 16 November killed one Chinese national and one Congolese police officer; gold was reportedly stolen.
events.body: Facts: Provinces 26 and Forum des As reported on 19 November 2026 that armed men attacked the Ndiyo gold-mining area in Mari-Minza chiefdom, Watsa territory, Haut-Uélé, around 07:00 on 16 November, killing one Chinese national and one Congolese police officer. Both reports cite local civil-society coordinator Célestin Kolongbe, who said the attackers removed a container of gold. Assessment: The reported theft alongside the killings favors the working hypothesis of organized mine-site robbery; deliberately targeting particular personnel remains an alternative for investigators. Operational impact: Gold custody and handover arrangements, predictable personnel movement and site protection are relevant exposures. Management: Account for Chinese employees and contractors near Watsa, subject gold transfers and non-essential visits in the affected area to special approval, review custody handovers and local police information. Indicators: Investigative findings, quantity stolen and mine operator, recurrence at nearby sites, changes in policing and gold transport practices. Verification: Two local reports citing the same civil-society source. Sources: https://provinces26rdc.com/haut-uele-un-ressortissant-chinois-et-un-policier-tues-dans-une-attaque-armee-dans-un-carre-minier/; https://www.forumdesas.cd/index.php/haut-uele-un-chinois-et-un-policier-tues-dans-une-attaque-armee

events.title: Pakistan Gwadar: Ten killed and 27 injured in Ormara coastal highway LPG tanker crash
events.summary: On 19 November, a passenger coach collided with an LPG tanker near Basol and Ormara on the Makran Coastal Highway, causing a fire that killed ten people and reportedly injured 27. Traffic was suspended for several hours.
events.body:
Facts: On 19 November, a passenger coach travelling from Turbat to Karachi collided with an LPG tanker near Basol in the Ormara area of Gwadar district. Both vehicles caught fire. Dawn cited Makran Coastal Highway police chief Muhammad Aslam Bangulzai confirming at least ten deaths, burn injuries and a highway closure lasting several hours. Hum English subsequently reported 27 injured, citing police. The N-10 coastal highway is geographically distinct from the N-40 route through Chagai and Nok Kundi.
Assessment: This is a high-consequence road transport incident involving mixed passenger and hazardous-material traffic. Repeated severe crashes on this corridor make driver conduct, hazardous cargo movement and medical response capability relevant operational concerns. The cause remains under police investigation; the incident is classified as transport safety and temporary logistics disruption, not an armed attack. Companies moving staff and freight between Gwadar, Ormara, Pasni, Turbat and Karachi face exposure through journey delays, vehicle selection, emergency evacuation arrangements and interaction with LPG tankers. Reports establish several hours of closure at the time, not an ongoing highway shutdown.
Operational response: Check current N-10 traffic notices and the precise incident location before dispatch; review contractor vehicle condition, driver hours and hazardous cargo separation practices; identify medical transfer contacts and alternate safe stops for the Ormara–Pasni section. Track three verifiable indicators: police findings on crash causation, official road clearance and reopening notices, and final casualty figures or regulatory changes affecting coach and tanker operations.
Sources: https://www.dawn.com/news/2045668; https://humenglish.com/latest/10-killed-27-injured-as-bus-collides-with-lpg-tanker-on-makran-coastal-highway/

events.title: Pakistan Khuzdar: Armed blockade reported on RCD Highway near Kuraro with commercial vehicles burned
events.summary: A local report dated 19 November describes armed checkpoints near Kuraro, several hours of disruption to the RCD Highway and commercial vehicles reportedly set on fire.
events.body: Facts: The Balochistan Post reported on 19 November that armed men erected checkpoints and searched vehicles on the RCD Highway near Kuraro in Khuzdar. Traffic was reportedly blocked for several hours, approaching Pakistani forces were reportedly ambushed and several commercial vehicles burned. Local administrators reportedly advised motorists to avoid the affected section. Assessment: Temporary road control affects freight through vehicle losses, carrier refusal and delays. It may signal a challenge to government transport control or a shorter localized raid. This is a distinct event from the Chagai mining-site seizure. Management: Reconcile drivers, shipments and vehicles, hold departures to the affected road section, and resume after verified local reopening. Indicators: Reopening, cargo and vehicle losses, responsibility claims and repeated roadblocks. Verification: single local-media report pending independent confirmation. Source: https://thebalochistanpost.net/2026/11/armed-men-attack-mining-site-in-chagai-and-block-highway-in-khuzdar/

events.title: Mali: Africa Corps expands Lancet strikes amid rising airstrike fatalities
events.summary: Reuters reported CIG findings on 19 November that Russian Africa Corps forces increased Lancet drone use in Mali, while ACLED-derived strike and fatality counts rose sharply after April.
events.body: Facts: Reuters reported a Conflict Insights Group assessment identifying at least ten strikes since April using ZALA Lancet loitering munitions with surveillance drones. CIG cited ACLED figures showing weekly recorded airstrikes rising from fewer than seven to almost sixteen and associated fatalities from fewer than 25 to over 60. CIG assessed that at least one strike almost certainly targeted a vehicle carrying civilians. Assessment: After the coordinated April insurgent offensive, Russian and Malian forces increased remote strikes to regain initiative. Greater strike capacity may bring tactical benefits but increases the importance of civilian vehicle identification and intelligence quality. An alternative explanation is that the larger battlefield and more targets explain the increased strike count. Business implications: Mining, energy and logistics operators in contested central and northern Mali should review route-specific exposure to aerial operations, field-vehicle authorisations, contractor movement, vehicle identification and stopping points. Indicators: strike locations and civilian harm, weekly ACLED trends, official investigations, carrier rerouting and insurance terms. Source: https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/russias-africa-corps-deploys-new-drone-mali-strikes-increase-analysis-says-2026-11-19/

events.title: DR Congo / Tanganyika | Two killed and Chinese national abducted on Kalemie–Bendera road
events.body: Facts \| On 14 November around midday, gunmen ambushed a vehicle associated with a Chinese business roughly 42 km from Kalemie on the Bendera road in Tanganyika province. Kalemie territory administrator John Mutombo Kabanga told Radio Okapi that two people were killed, including a FARDC soldier assigned to protection and a mining-company employee. The driver suffered a gunshot injury and one Chinese national was abducted into the bush. The search continued when the story was reported on 17 November. Event date: 14 November; reporting date: 17 November. Assessment \| The attack places the most immediate exposure outside the mine, on the road linking operations and supporting infrastructure. The death of the escorting soldier shows that the vehicle's armed protection was overwhelmed. Previous kidnappings involving foreign mining personnel on roads near Kalemie suggest that repeated journeys may offer armed groups predictable opportunities. Both opportunistic interception and deliberate selection of a foreign target remain plausible; the attackers' identity and motive are under investigation. Bendera power-facility rehabilitation may create additional technician movements along the corridor, although no interruption to the rehabilitation has been established. Business implications \| Mining, engineering and energy operators using the Kalemie–Bendera corridor should reauthorise non-essential road journeys, review actual routes and escort capacity, test emergency communications and medical evacuation times, and coordinate employer and consular responses for the hostage. Businesses dependent on Bendera rehabilitation should check contractor attendance and delivery schedules individually. Indicators \| (1) Hostage recovery and condition; (2) identification and motive of the attackers; (3) actual road access and further attacks; (4) changes to Bendera maintenance personnel movements and logistics. Sources \| [Radio Okapi, 17 Nov 2026](https://www.radiookapi.net/2026/11/17/actualite/securite/un-ressortissant-chinois-enleve-et-deux-morts-dans-une-embuscade-sur); [RTNC, 17 Nov 2026](https://rtnc.cd/tanganyika-embuscade-meurtriere-sur-laxe-kalemie-bendera/); [Nzadi News, 17 Nov 2026](https://nzadinews.net/kalemie-un-ressortissant-chinois-enleve-et-deux-morts-dans-une-embuscade-sur-laxe-bendera/). Verification: named local administrator and multiple reports; perpetrator identity pending.

events.title: Guinea / Siguiri | 224 sentenced in illegal-gold crackdown as miners move across borders
events.body: Facts \| AP reported on 17 November that a Siguiri court sentenced 202 miners to three years in prison and 22 former local officials to two years. Foreign defendants also face ten-year exclusion orders. The crackdown follows 11 November clashes in Balato that killed ten and injured thirteen, with over 1,200 people detained. Miners and families have crossed into Mali. Assessment \| Enforcement has shifted from site clearance to criminal punishment and cross-border displacement. The government's environmental and formal gold-revenue objectives collide with livelihoods built around informal extraction. The leading hypothesis is an attempt to restructure control of gold production and revenue; a narrower alternative is a temporary response to pollution and recent violence. Receiving communities in Mali face labour, humanitarian and security pressures, while licensed operators face changing community and procurement conditions. Management implications \| Operators around Siguiri should audit subcontracted extraction and mineral sourcing, identify any detained personnel requiring legal assistance and map enforcement boundaries. Businesses near Mali's border should reassess staff exposure at transport and temporary-settlement nodes. Indicators \| (1) Appeals and deportation enforcement; (2) actual arrivals and resettlement in Mali; (3) new licence and sourcing rules; (4) protests or clashes around Siguiri. Sources \| [AP, 17 Nov 2026](https://apnews.com/article/0cdc24ae7e2c34bfff28201dd73ba293); [Guardian, 17 Nov 2026](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/17/guinea-mining-crackdown-illgal-exodus-sahel). Verification: court outcomes reported; displacement estimates vary.

events.title: Bulgaria / Black Sea | LPG carrier Gas Husky sinks; all 19 crew rescued
events.body: Facts \| Reuters reported on 17 November that the Liberian-flagged LPG carrier Gas Husky sank roughly 50 miles east of Byala, Bulgaria, carrying about 3,400 tonnes of LPG. All 19 crew were rescued. Bulgaria's Defence Ministry confirmed the vessel disappeared from radar and activated a distress beacon. The cause is under investigation. events.title: Russia / Crimea | Kerch Bridge road span damaged, road traffic suspended as rail service resumes
events.body: Facts \| On 17 November Ukraine said it struck the Kerch Bridge for a second day, collapsing a road arch and span and damaging the railway section. Russian officials acknowledged structural damage; the Russian-installed Crimean governor reported two deaths and suspended road traffic. Rail services later resumed and motorists were directed to ferries. Reuters also reported strikes on Kyiv bridges and energy infrastructure, with outages in eight Ukrainian regions. Assessment \| Both sides are increasing pressure on transport and energy nodes while territorial negotiations remain stalled. Damage to the Kerch road connection creates immediate logistical friction; debris may also affect Sea of Azov navigation. Russian strikes on Kyiv bridges and energy assets impose parallel civilian and industrial costs. The leading explanation is pressure on the opponent's logistics and negotiating position, with near-term military retaliation an alternative. Road closure, restored rail services and maritime implications require separate operational decisions. Business implications \| Operators exposed to Crimea, the Sea of Azov or Ukrainian transport networks should verify road and rail service notices, ferry capacity, navigation restrictions and contract-delay exposure. Energy-dependent Ukrainian operations should update production and staff plans against actual restoration reports. Indicators \| (1) Bridge structural assessments and road reopening; (2) Sea of Azov clearance notices; (3) actual rail capacity; (4) power restoration across affected Ukrainian regions. Sources \| [Reuters, 17 Nov 2026](https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukraine-strikes-crimean-bridge-second-day-russia-pounds-kyiv-bridges-2026-11-17/); [AP, 17 Nov 2026](https://apnews.com/article/df4b867cf8f70e88843d8fefea5d643c). events.body: Facts \| UKMTO reported on 17 November that a tanker was struck again approximately seven nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, causing a fire; its crew was unaccounted for. events.title: Nigeria / Bauchi | Chinese mining exploration worker and police escort killed in ambush
events.body: Facts \| At approximately 1:30 p.m. on 14 November, gunmen ambushed a mining survey and core-drilling team near Ruga village, Gwana district, Alkaleri LGA, Bauchi State. Chinese national Wang Tingjian, aged 37, and police escort Inspector Abba Ya'u were killed. Channels Television reported on 16 November that Bauchi police spokesperson SP Nafiu Habib confirmed the attack and identified Zurfi Mining Company as the worker's employer. Police, military and local security personnel are pursuing the attackers. Assessment \| The incident demonstrates material exposure during exploration, before commercial production begins. Survey and drilling crews travel to dispersed work sites and can develop predictable movements. The death of an assigned police escort shows that the existing protection arrangement was penetrated. Opportunistic violence against an identifiable foreign worker and a planned attack on mining activity are competing explanations; police findings will determine attribution and motive. Business implications \| Exploration and drilling operators in Bauchi and nearby areas should review non-essential field movements, site-access routes, vehicle tasking, escort availability, extraction plans and medical evacuation arrangements. Managers linked to Zurfi Mining should confirm personnel accountability, contractor activity, investigation status and family support. The incident requires a reassessment of single-vehicle fieldwork exposure and operating thresholds. Indicators \| (1) Police identification of perpetrators and motive; (2) operational changes by Zurfi Mining or related projects; (3) further attacks on survey convoys around Gwana; (4) new police or mining-regulator restrictions. events.title: Bulgaria / Black Sea | Grain carrier Betul 8 sinks as maritime drone threat spreads along western routes
events.body: Facts \| On 16 November, the Somali-flagged Betul 8 sank in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone about 40 nautical miles southeast of Cape Kaliakra. The vessel was carrying approximately 3,000 tonnes of wheat from Tulcea, Romania, to Egypt. All 12 crew were rescued. Bulgaria confirmed the sinking and rescue. Crew members reported strikes by two unmanned surface vessels; maritime-security sources gave Reuters a similar account. The attacker has not been established. AP identified the crew as eight Turkish and four Azerbaijani nationals. Assessment \| The significance is the spread of ship losses into commercial routes off Bulgaria and Romania. Repeated small-scale attacks can disrupt grain exports through crew reluctance, war-risk insurance, rejected voyages and port congestion without a comprehensive blockade. The leading hypothesis is an attempt to increase the cost of third-country shipping. Targeting errors or localised actions remain plausible alternatives. Exposure should be assessed by vessel and sea area. Business implications \| Grain, mineral and equipment shippers using Romanian or Ukrainian Black Sea ports should reassess carrier acceptance, war-risk exclusions, loading arrangements and alternative ports on a voyage basis. Egyptian buyers should verify cargo losses, replacement procurement and delivery dates. Management should set explicit voyage-risk tolerances and inventory buffers. Indicators \| (1) Bulgarian forensic findings on unmanned surface vessels; (2) further incidents near Sulina and the Bulgarian coast; (3) war-risk premiums and actual sailing schedules; (4) implementation of the EU Black Sea maritime-security hub. events.title: Sudan / Ethiopia | Mutual accusations of backing armed groups raise risk of a cross-border proxy conflict
events.body: Facts \| AP reported on 16 November that Sudan's military accused Ethiopia of permitting Rapid Support Forces (RSF) camps, drone operations and cross-border attacks, and had filed complaints with the UN and African Union. Ethiopia accused Sudan of backing Tigrayan rebels and expelled six Sudanese consular staff in Asosa, closing the mission. Both sides deny the accusations. Satellite research by Yale's Humanitarian Research Lab identified a military buildup near Asosa associated with the RSF. Assessment \| Sudan's civil war and renewed Tigray fighting are becoming linked through border access, drone operations and diplomatic retaliation. Sudan's military seeks to constrain RSF supply and manoeuvre; Ethiopia is concerned about outside support for its Tigrayan opponents. The leading hypothesis is growing use of armed proxies to stretch the neighbouring government. Alternatively, mutual accusations may remain diplomatic pressure without sustained cross-border operations. The Al-Fashaga territorial dispute and Nile dam politics raise the cost of compromise. Business implications \| Operators in eastern Sudan and western Ethiopia should reassess specific border crossings, administrative restrictions, evacuation routes and supply nodes. Escalation around Blue Nile and Asosa could affect personnel movement, project cargo and emergency response simultaneously. Investors should assess border security separately from dam-related political risks. Indicators \| (1) New satellite evidence of camps and drone operations; (2) border closures, expulsions or military deployments; (3) cross-border clashes involving Tigray or eastern Sudan; (4) verifiable AU or UN mediation measures. Source \| [AP, 16 Nov 2026](https://apnews.com/article/sudan-rsf-ethiopia-tigray-war-649640494d674bfffcdc4418205b7485). events.title: European Union / Russia | Financial and energy-linked sanctions expand as winter infrastructure strikes continue
events.body: Facts \| On 16 November, EU foreign ministers imposed sanctions on nearly 50 Russian banks and financial institutions and targeted individuals linked to energy and oil trade, with further asset freezes and travel bans relating to alleged disinformation. EU officials accused Russia of prolonging peace talks while striking Ukrainian power infrastructure. AP reported disagreement over a proposed new European security framework following recent Abu Dhabi talks. Assessment \| The EU is combining financial restrictions, energy-trade compliance and diplomatic pressure to increase the cost of Russia's war during winter infrastructure attacks. Moscow's broader security-framework demands may seek to move negotiations from a Ukrainian ceasefire to the European security order; alternatively, high initial demands may serve as bargaining leverage. The operational impact lies in named sanctioned entities and payment, insurance and intermediary relationships. Business implications \| Firms transacting with Russian banks, energy traders or logistics intermediaries should review the formal sanctions list against counterparties, beneficial owners, payment routes, termination provisions and cargo already in transit. Companies dependent on Ukrainian energy and rail networks should reflect winter disruption in delivery planning. Prioritise contracts vulnerable to payment freezes or loss of insurance cover. Indicators \| (1) EU legal texts and named entities; (2) payment rejections and energy-shipping compliance changes; (3) concrete ceasefire provisions; (4) Ukrainian electricity infrastructure damage and restoration. Source \| [AP, 16 Nov 2026](https://apnews.com/article/europe-ukraine-russia-security-ceasefire-cde686fba0e452b10ca613b3517e884e). Verification: EU actions and ministerial statements reported; negotiating intent is analytical inference.

events.title: Ukraine / Black Sea and energy infrastructure | Communications restrictions affect interceptor drones as strikes damage gas infrastructure
events.body: Facts \| Associated Press reported on 15 November that President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Starshield communications restrictions caused high-speed interceptor drones to lose contact with operators, weakening Ukraine's defence against Russian drones. A strike on Chornomorsk injured six people, damaged energy facilities and a gas pipeline, and temporarily cut electricity to approximately 41,000 customers. Romania separately reported drone strikes on three Black Sea commercial vessels without reported casualties. These are Ukrainian and Romanian official accounts reported by AP; the technical mechanism behind the communications restrictions requires clarification from the provider. Assessment \| The incidents illustrate how winter energy resilience depends on both physical protection and communications continuity. Attacks on power, gas and port assets can compound disruption through repairs, outages and delayed cargo handling. If interceptor systems rely on a particular satellite communications service, restrictions may amplify the effect. An alternative explanation is that some failures result from speed, integration or local network conditions alongside any policy or service restrictions affecting defensive systems. Attacks on commercial ships also widen exposure to third-country operators. Business implications \| Companies dependent on Ukrainian power, gas or Chornomorsk cargo handling should check actual operator restoration notices and delivery schedules. Black Sea shippers should reassess specific vessels, routes and war-risk terms. Operators relying on a single communications provider should verify service constraints, fallback links and tested failover arrangements. Indicators \| (1) Whether Starshield and Ukrainian authorities announce changes to restrictions; (2) restoration of Chornomorsk energy and port assets; (3) identification and damage assessments for the commercial vessels; (4) whether subsequent strikes continue targeting winter energy systems. Source \| [Associated Press, 15 November 2026](https://apnews.com/article/b139307f0d3ed0f7d0b222c08c30a4a1). events.title: Iran / Ilam | Oil and gas workers' bus overturns, killing at least 12
events.body: Facts \| Iranian state media reported that a bus transporting oil and gas company employees overturned late on 14 November in western Ilam Province, killing at least 12 people and injuring 16. The account was carried by international media on 15 November. Local authorities are investigating. The operator, exact route and vehicle condition have not been identified in the available report. Assessment \| This major incident directly concerns workforce transport safety. Concentrated shift travel, road conditions, vehicle maintenance and driver working hours can turn a single crash into a mass-casualty event. The investigation needs to establish the roles of vehicle condition, driver behaviour and road hazards. The operational question is whether the same carrier or route exposes other employee groups to a repeatable failure. Business implications \| Oil and gas operators arranging staff buses in Ilam and neighbouring areas should review contracted carriers, fleet condition, night-driving schedules, driver rosters and emergency response coverage on the affected routes. Operators using the same carrier or road should prioritise a targeted journey and vehicle review. Any effect on production remains unknown. Indicators \| (1) Police investigation findings; (2) identification of the company, carrier and route; (3) suspension or modification of staff transport; (4) any regional inspection programme for similar buses. Source \| [Times of India citing Iranian state media, 15 November 2026](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/middle-east/12-killed-16-injured-as-bus-carrying-oil-and-gas-workers-overturns-in-iran/articleshow/135850125.cms). events.title: Yemen / Bab el-Mandeb | Government forces withdraw from Dhubab, leaving strategic coastline under Houthi control
events.body: Facts \| Reuters reported on 15 November that forces aligned with Yemen's internationally recognised, Saudi-backed government announced their withdrawal from Dhubab Airport and positions near Bab el-Mandeb, west of Taiz, redeploying toward Aden. The withdrawal leaves the Houthis controlling territory overlooking the strategic strait. The coastal control change is confirmed; commercial navigation and any formal closure require separate verification. Assessment \| The government's stated rationale is to reinforce Aden and other fronts, consistent with pressure on its force allocation and logistics. For the Houthis, the coastline offers leverage over a shipping route connecting Asia, Europe and the Suez Canal. The leading hypothesis is that territorial gains strengthen Houthi bargaining power with Saudi Arabia, the Yemeni government and shipping interests. An alternative is a deliberate government shortening of its defensive line without a proportional improvement in Houthi capability to impose a sustained maritime blockade. Territorial control and operational interdiction capability are distinct. Business implications \| Cargo owners using the Red Sea and Suez route should reassess specific voyages, flag exposure, charter and war-risk clauses, Cape of Good Hope alternatives, delivery lead times and inventory buffers. Do not treat the withdrawal alone as proof of a strait closure. Yemen-linked projects should review control of their actual access routes and port interfaces and assess restrictions at each location. Indicators \| (1) Durability of Houthi control near Dhubab; (2) new UKMTO or shipowner incident reports; (3) Suez transits, insurance pricing and carrier routing decisions; (4) any government counteroffensive from Aden. Source \| [Reuters, 15 November 2026](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/yemen-government-forces-withdraw-area-near-bab-el-mandeb-strait-houthis-control-2026-11-15/). events.title: Pakistan / Chagai | Mari Energies reports East Siah Diq copper-gold discovery adjacent to Siah Diq project
events.body: Facts \| On 13 November, Mari Energies disclosed to the Pakistan Stock Exchange a porphyry-style copper-gold discovery at East Siah Diq (ESD-1), through its wholly owned subsidiary Mari Minerals. Approximately 25,000 metres have been drilled across two phases, identifying mineralisation over roughly 1.4 sq km. Mari Minerals still needs Phase 1B assays, deeper drilling, metallurgical work and resource modelling to establish continuity and economic viability. A plausible outcome is increased exploration and contractor activity around Nokkundi; an alternative is that subsequent results do not support a commercially viable project. Ownership, licence boundaries and infrastructure sharing with Siah Diq require examination of separate corporate and regulatory records. Operational and management implications \| Operators around Siah Diq, Reko Diq and Nokkundi should treat this as a material neighbouring-project development, with its near-term relevance focused on exploration and project interfaces. Map publicly disclosed licence boundaries and potential interfaces involving exploration access, water, power, contractors and community employment. Reassess personnel and journey exposure only if new drilling campaigns, camps or transport movements are actually announced. Indicators \| (1) Phase 1B assay results expected in Q1 2027; (2) a compliant mineral resource estimate and metallurgical recovery data; (3) new drilling, road or camp procurement; (4) official disclosures on licence boundaries, community engagement and infrastructure arrangements. events.title: Poland / Qatar | Orlen terminates long-term Qatari LNG contract as conflict reshapes procurement economics
events.body: Facts \| Reuters reported on 13 November that Poland's Orlen terminated a 2009 contract for approximately one million tonnes of Qatari LNG annually through 2034, about 14 cargoes per year. The company cited QatarEnergy's force majeure following Iranian attacks on Qatari facilities. Termination takes effect after 60 days without penalty. A separate Qatari contract remains in place, alongside Norwegian and US supply. Analysts estimated potential savings of \$1.7–2 billion, contingent on replacement costs. Assessment \| This is a second-order commercial consequence of infrastructure damage: force majeure can change the economics and survival of long-term supply agreements, and reduce the availability of spot cargoes. Orlen's diversified sourcing may let it exit an expensive oil-indexed contract, but higher replacement prices could erase part of the projected benefit. Business implications \| LNG buyers should review force-majeure notices, termination rights, alternative pricing and shipping slots. This contract termination does not itself establish Polish supply shortages or a complete halt in Qatari exports. Indicators \| (1) disputes during the 60-day notice period; (2) Orlen's replacement suppliers and prices; (3) QatarEnergy's recovery and contractual performance; (4) European LNG spreads and freight rates. Source \| [Reuters, 13 November 2026](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/dropping-qatar-lng-deal-seen-saving-polands-orlen-up-2-billion-2026-11-13/). Verification: reported company decision; projected savings are estimates.

events.title: United States | Nationwide FAA air-traffic communications outage halts departures and disrupts aviation logistics
events.body: Facts \| At around 4 p.m. Eastern on 13 November, the Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop for departing flights following a serious air-traffic-control communications outage. Aircraft already airborne were managed under safety procedures, while international departures were addressed individually. The Transportation Secretary said regional control centres were affected. At the time of initial reports, the cause and full recovery timetable were unknown. The Homeland Security Secretary said there was no evidence at that point of malicious activity. Reported delay and cancellation totals were evolving snapshots, not final counts. Assessment \| This is a common-mode failure of nationally important air-traffic communications affecting air-traffic communications across multiple airports. Restricting new departures reduces exposure while controllers lack reliable communications. Commercial disruption propagates into the next day through aircraft and crew displacement, duty-time limits, international connections and time-sensitive air freight. Aging infrastructure remains a hypothesis to be tested through the investigation; there is no basis yet to attribute the outage to cyberattack or newly deployed software. Business implications \| Employers with US travel, connecting flights, urgent technical staff movements or critical spare-parts shipments should check individual flight and cargo status directly with carriers and assess next-day crew, aircraft and shipment availability. Where delivery or mobilisation deadlines are critical, managers should compare confirmed alternative flights, ground transfers and contractual deadlines before activating contingencies. Indicators \| (1) FAA withdrawal of the nationwide ground stop and residual restrictions; (2) airline cancellation and recovery rates; (3) international connection and air-cargo backlogs; (4) formal FAA root-cause and communications-redundancy findings. Sources \| [Reuters, 13 November 2026](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/faa-issues-national-ground-stop-due-extraordinary-circumstance-reasons-safety-2026-11-13/); [AP, 13 November 2026](https://apnews.com/article/6aaa6bd4991ef22eb0c3baa6961a91d1). Verification: FAA and US official announcements reported by multiple outlets; cause and recovery status evolving.

events.title: Egypt | Proposed state-backed licensing of artisanal gold mining raises questions over foreign detainees
events.body: Facts \| Reuters reported on 13 November that Aswan lawmaker Mona Shaker described a proposal for a company under the Future of Egypt Authority to license artisanal gold miners and release certain people detained for illegal prospecting. The military previously reported detaining 151 Egyptians and 540 foreigners since June. No formal decision establishing the company or specifying whether foreign detainees would be released was reported. Assessment \| The proposal could shift informal mining into a state-linked licensing and revenue system, potentially reducing enforcement friction while strengthening government control over access. An alternative is that it remains a preliminary political accommodation whose legal implementation remains pending. The status of any releases or issued licences should be checked against official administrative records. Business implications \| Mining and exploration companies should distinguish existing concessions from the proposed artisanal regime, review legal representation for any detained staff and check concession overlaps and local subcontractor exposure. A new licensing authority could materially change access negotiations and counterparties. Indicators \| (1) Published legal instrument and licensing body; (2) confirmed releases, including any foreign nationals; (3) changes in illegal mining interference with concessions; (4) revised licence, fee or concession rules. Source \| [Reuters, 13 November 2026](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/egypt-set-up-state-backed-company-license-artisanal-gold-miners-free-detainees-2026-11-13/). events.title: Saudi Arabia / Yemen | Houthis claim ballistic missile attack in Jazan amid pressure on Red Sea energy routes
events.body: Facts \| On 13 November, the Houthis claimed to have fired two ballistic missiles at Saudi forces in Al-Tuwal, Jazan. Business implications \| Companies in Jazan should check actual civil-defence warnings, site restrictions and border movements. Crude buyers dependent on Yanbu should separately verify pipeline throughput and vessel loadings, using separate checks for military incidents and actual pipeline operations. Indicators \| (1) Saudi confirmation of impact sites and damage; (2) repeated Jazan warnings; (3) Yanbu loadings and pipeline throughput; (4) further linked Houthi military and energy claims. events.title: Iran / Strait of Hormuz | Iran reports gas carrier mine explosion amid contested shipping restrictions
events.body: Facts \| On 13 November, Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said a vessel carrying liquefied gas struck a naval mine and exploded in the Strait of Hormuz while using a route Tehran described as unauthorised and dangerous. Reuters reported that the vessel's identity was unavailable. Reports differ in referring to LNG and LPG; the cargo, vessel, casualties and damage must not yet be treated as established. Iran separately reported explosions involving four oil tankers on the preceding days, requiring vessel-level deduplication. Assessment \| The announcement reinforces Iran's attempt to exercise practical control over routes and passage permissions. If the mine incident is substantiated, operators face linked navigational, insurance and voyage-acceptance constraints. A credible alternative is deterrent signalling through a claim whose physical consequences remain unclear. The strait's operating status should be established from maritime and port authorities. Business implications \| Energy buyers and carriers should obtain the vessel name, IMO number, confirmed cargo, track, owner and insurer instructions, and reconcile delivery windows and war-risk costs against contract obligations. LNG and LPG exposure must be distinguished before making supply-disruption assumptions. Indicators \| (1) UKMTO, flag-state or owner identification and damage confirmation; (2) verifiable AIS and rescue records; (3) changes to designated routes or transit approvals; (4) sustained shifts in gas-carrier traffic and war-risk pricing. Sources \| [Reuters, 13 Nov 2026](https://www.reuters.com/world/iran-says-tanker-carrying-lng-hit-mine-suffered-explosion-hormuz-2026-11-13/); [AP, 13 Nov 2026](https://apnews.com/article/5d73a23b5b8647d2515c35b267b36c08). events.title: Bahrain / Iran | IRGC claims strike on US early-warning radar, raising Gulf escalation concerns
events.body: Facts \| On 13 November, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation for what Iran described as an airstrike on telecommunications infrastructure in Sirik, Hormozgan province. Iranian media claimed the radar was destroyed. At the time of Reuters' report, neither the US nor Bahrain had confirmed damage. Bahrain hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet headquarters. Assessment \| Publicly claiming a strike against US warning infrastructure in a Gulf host state may be intended to link attacks on Iranian coastal assets to the security of US regional bases, increasing the political cost of further strikes. An alternative is deterrent messaging with limited physical effect. Confirmation of damage or a military response would materially change the assessment. Business implications \| Bahrain-based employers and regional carriers should review actual civil aviation, port and civil-defence restrictions, staff movements and shelter arrangements. Civil aviation authorities' notices are needed to determine the actual scope of any airspace closure. The nature of any subsequent US-Iran exchange will determine whether risks spread to coastal energy and shipping facilities. Indicators \| (1) US or Bahraini confirmation of damage or casualties; (2) new airspace, port or civil-defence restrictions; (3) further direct military exchanges; (4) new Gulf diplomatic de-escalation measures. Sources \| [Reuters, 13 Nov 2026](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/irans-guards-say-they-targeted-us-early-warning-radar-bahrain-2026-11-13/); [Al Jazeera, 13 Nov 2026](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/13/iran-says-it-struck-us-radar-site-in-bahrain). events.title: Russia / Volgograd | Drone strike on industrial zone kills four; refinery impact unresolved
events.body: Facts \| On 13 November, regional governor Andrei Bocharov said a Ukrainian drone attack on Volgograd's industrial zone killed four people and injured two. The city hosts a major Lukoil refinery and other industrial facilities. Social-media footage purportedly showed a refinery fire, but authorities did not confirm that the refinery was hit. Reuters reported wider temporary disruption to Russian refining capacity from recent attacks, citing industry sources. Assessment \| Industrial-zone casualties have an official local source; damage to refinery processing units remains the critical missing fact. Confirmed refinery damage would place the event within the ongoing campaign against Russian fuel-processing and logistics capacity. Damage confined to other industrial premises would have materially different implications. The presence of a refinery in the city is insufficient evidence of a refinery outage. Business implications \| Contractors should establish the precise affected site, account for personnel and verify industrial and rail operations. Fuel buyers should rely on operator disclosures and observed unit utilisation before incorporating a Volgograd refinery loss into supply assumptions. Indicators \| (1) Lukoil confirmation of unit damage; (2) updated governor casualty and site reports; (3) refinery utilisation and rail fuel shipments; (4) repeat strikes in the same industrial area. Source \| [Reuters, 13 Nov 2026](https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/four-killed-ukrainian-drone-strike-industrial-zone-russias-volgograd-official-2026-11-13/). events.title: DR Congo / Lualaba | Armed robbery of mining convoy on Kisanfu–Kisankala corridor
events.body: Facts \| [Actualite.cd](http://Actualite.cd) reported on 13 November that around six armed men intercepted a convoy of mining operators on 12 November along the Kisanfu–Kisankala road in Mutshatsha territory, taking cash and belongings. Perpetrator attribution for each incident remains a separate investigative question. Predictable movements, cash carriage and uneven policing are possible explanations requiring incident-level evidence. Business implications \| Operators using the road should reconcile the affected journey and victim identities, separate cash movement from routine staff transport where feasible and make journey decisions on actual police reporting and road conditions. A province-wide mining transport shutdown is not established. Indicators \| (1) Police identification of vehicles and suspects; (2) further robberies or abductions on the corridor; (3) changes in cash movement practices; (4) actual road restrictions or policing changes. events.title: Pakistan / Balochistan | Vehicle-borne bomb attack on Mastung N-25 FC checkpoint kills civilians
events.body: Facts \| On 12 November, attackers used an explosives-laden vehicle against Kandawa Post on the N-25 near Mastung. Police statements carried by Radio Pakistan reported two civilian deaths, three attackers killed in the ensuing response, at least 13 civilians injured and three FC personnel wounded. Assessment \| The attack demonstrates continued capacity to use vehicle-borne explosives against fixed security positions, while conditions across the rest of the province require separate assessment. It also illustrates collateral exposure around military checkpoints. Mastung's N-25 must not be confused with Chagai's N-40; no N-40 closure or change in Chagai escorts is established. Business implications \| Operators travelling via Mastung should check checkpoint-area traffic controls and avoid unnecessary waiting close to potential military targets. Chagai project teams should incorporate the incident into province-wide VBIED trend analysis without inventing local movement restrictions. Indicators \| (1) Final police casualty and damage report; (2) corroboration of the BLA attribution; (3) actual N-25 restrictions and reopening; (4) repeat VBIED attacks on FC positions. Business implications \| Mining and equipment contractors in Region One should check overlaps between concessions and indigenous land title, suspend disputed equipment entry absent clear authorisation and retain records of community consultation. Do not misclassify this as anti-Chinese violence. events.title: Saudi Arabia | Houthis claim strikes on East-West oil pipeline and Yanbu energy facilities
events.body: Facts \| On 12 November, Yemen's Houthis claimed drone and missile strikes against a pumping station on Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline, energy infrastructure at Yanbu and a Saudi Aramco building in Riyadh, without specifying the dates of each alleged strike. A credible alternative is signalling intended to maximise political pressure despite limited physical damage. Available evidence confirms an ongoing threat; pipeline operating status requires operator confirmation. Business implications \| Exposure centres on Yanbu loading schedules, Red Sea shipping, crude supply contracts and war-risk insurance. Buyers should verify actual loading ports, contractual delivery windows, vessel routes and alternative supply capacity and verify any outage against operator data. Indicators \| (1) Saudi Aramco or ministry confirmation of damage or throughput loss; (2) delays in Yanbu loading; (3) repeated strikes on pumping stations or Red Sea terminals; (4) sustained changes in tanker war-risk premiums and freight costs. events.title: Oman / Strait of Hormuz | Reported strike on Didamar navigation systems raises maritime infrastructure risk
events.body: Facts \| Reuters reported on 11 November, citing three sources, that Iran struck ship-navigation systems on Oman's Didamar island. The likely effect, if the strike occurred as reported, is increased uncertainty and potentially greater route-management costs; a single damaged aid with functional backups may have little operational impact. Repeated interference at multiple sites would represent a materially different scenario. events.title: Guinea / Siguiri | Fatal clashes over artisanal gold mining ban leave 10 dead and 13 injured
events.body: Facts \| Guinea's government reported clashes on 11 November in Balato, Siguiri, during enforcement of a 2 November ban on artisanal gold mining. Ten people died, including five foreigners whose nationalities were not disclosed, and 13 were injured. Protesters blocked a patrol and gunfire followed; investigators have not established who fired first. The crackdown has also driven cross-border movement into Mali and repatriations to Burkina Faso. Assessment \| Authorities seek to curb environmental damage and reassert control over gold production, while enforcement threatens livelihoods dependent on artisanal mining. A mismatch between coercive enforcement and livelihood alternatives is a strong explanation for unrest; organised resistance by local illicit mining interests is another possibility that requires evidence. Foreign victims must not be presumed Chinese. Business implications \| Gold-sector firms should verify licences, ore provenance, workforce and transport subcontractors, and the precise enforcement footprint. Cross-border displacement may affect transport, accommodation and informal labour markets in Mali and Burkina Faso. Mining operations elsewhere in Guinea and any effects on Simandou need separate verification. Indicators \| (1) Judicial findings on gunfire and victims' nationalities; (2) changes to the mining ban; (3) repatriation and displacement numbers; (4) documented interruptions at licensed mines. Sources \| [Reuters, 13 November 2026](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/10-killed-clashes-guinea-after-artisanal-mining-ban-2026-11-13/); [AP, 13 November 2026](https://apnews.com/article/3bf55251d4da7159b04e031c8783d7a4). Verification: government casualty figures carried by multiple outlets; responsibility under investigation.

events.title: UAE | Tanker struck off Ras Al-Khaimah; 22 crew evacuated
events.body: Facts \| On 11 November, maritime agencies reported that Liberia-flagged tanker DOMINICA PROSPERITY was struck by an unidentified projectile approximately 14 nautical miles northwest of Ras Al-Khaimah, causing an engine-room fire. India's shipping minister reported the safe evacuation of all 22 crew, including 19 Indian nationals. The incident occurred near Mina Saqr after the vessel had exited the Strait of Hormuz. No perpetrator has been identified. Assessment \| The location extends merchant-vessel exposure into UAE coastal approaches beyond the Strait itself. Engine-room damage and full evacuation directly removed this tanker from service. Regional conflict provides the relevant context, while the scope of any broader campaign and port restrictions depends on subsequent maritime reporting. Business implications \| Immediate effects concern crew safety, hull damage, claims and voyage disruption. Energy and industrial cargo operators using Ras Al-Khaimah, Fujairah and nearby approaches should verify vessel-specific positions, berth windows, war-risk cover and contingency delivery arrangements. There is no basis for assuming all UAE ports are closed. Indicators \| (1) Investigation of projectile type and origin; (2) firefighting, towing and any navigation restrictions; (3) further attacks in adjacent waters; (4) changes in war-risk premiums and vessel routing. Source \| [Reuters, 12 November](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/vessel-fire-after-being-struck-off-uaes-ras-al-khaimah-maritime-agencies-say-2026-11-12/), citing maritime agencies and India's shipping minister. events.title: Libya | Fatal explosion at Marsa Brega gas complex raises maintenance-funding concerns
events.body: Facts \| Libya's National Oil Corporation (NOC) said on 11 November that a fire and explosion at subsidiary Sirte Oil Company's Marsa Brega gas complex killed one worker and injured four. NOC chairman Massoud Soleman said preliminary evidence pointed to a leak in a boiler gas-supply line, with repairs expected to take at least two weeks. The affected plant was shut as a precaution, but NOC reported no interruption to domestic gas supplies or crude production. A local shutdown must not be equated with a national production loss. Assessment \| The key signal is the chairman's explicit link between delayed budget disbursement, postponed maintenance and the accident. This raises a testable asset-integrity hypothesis: sustained maintenance backlogs could increase worker exposure, downtime and contractor costs. A one-off component or operational failure remains a credible alternative; any systemic deterioration would require additional maintenance and reliability evidence. Business implications \| Immediate exposure lies in plant repair, isolation and contractor permits. As NOC reports uninterrupted supply, nationwide gas-disruption assumptions are unwarranted. Energy service providers should identify their actual contractual exposure and verify maintenance funding, isolation controls and restart conditions. Indicators \| (1) Final cause of the leak; (2) whether the two-week repair estimate slips or supply is affected; (3) disclosures on overdue maintenance funding; (4) comparable failures at other facilities. events.body: Facts \| At about 06:05 on 10 November, a road-construction camp in Mvumoni, Somangila, Kigamboni, Dar es Salaam, suffered extensive property damage. Dar es Salaam police said on 11 November that excavator operator Halidi Seleman Kalaghe, 45, allegedly drove the machine into gates, fencing, temporary accommodation and vehicles, including a Toyota Sienta and a company fuel tanker, following a dispute with his employer, China Energy Engineering Group Guanxi Hydroelectric Construction Bureau Co. Ltd. Police arrested the operator and initiated legal proceedings. The case remains at the allegation and investigation stage; criminal liability rests with the courts. Assessment \| The distinctive risk is the use of an authorised category of heavy equipment against the site's own facilities. Access to machinery and operating skills may turn an individual employment dispute into major asset damage in minutes. The police account supports an employment-related insider-damage hypothesis; the nature of the dispute, prior warning signs and equipment-start authorisation remain to be established. The police account currently describes an employment-linked incident involving insider damage. Business implications \| Damage to the perimeter, accommodation and fuel vehicle could disrupt access, housing, fuel delivery and work schedules. Before restarting affected equipment, management should review operator permissions, keys, parking controls and separation between heavy machinery, living quarters and fuel assets. Serious labour disputes warrant a documented review of machine-operation authorisations. Ordinary fencing is not designed to stop a deliberately driven excavator. Indicators \| (1) Police and court findings on motive, liability and loss; (2) work suspension and reopening dates; (3) revised machine authorisation and parking controls; (4) signs of broader labour mobilisation. A contained individual incident and effective remediation would limit the consequences; wider labour mobilisation would increase schedule and personnel exposure. events.title: DR Congo | At least 22 killed and 10 abducted in attacks on eight Mambasa communities, Ituri
events.body: Facts \| Between 10 and 11 November, armed attackers struck eight communities in the Babila-Teturi area of Mambasa territory, Ituri province. Local child and women's rights monitor APDEF reported at least 22 civilians killed, 10 abducted and one injured, with two motorcycles and five houses burned. Local groups attributed the attacks to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF). Associated Press interviewed civil society representatives and a local administrator on 11 November. Casualty figures remain provisional. Assessment \| The attacks across eight settlements in a short period demonstrate the armed group's ability to move between remote communities without timely interdiction. The ADF has long exploited forested terrain, limited access and weak state services near the DRC–Uganda border. A plausible hypothesis is that repeated attacks sustain fear and undermine confidence in public security; an alternative is opportunistic violence by smaller units operating where interception capacity is limited. There is no basis yet to infer a specific campaign against mining operators. Business implications \| Exposure is most immediate for local employees, subcontractors, road transport and medical evacuation in remote parts of Mambasa. Companies operating in eastern Ituri should map actual worksite proximity to the affected villages, reassess overnight stays and discretionary ground movements, and check personnel-accountability and missing-person escalation times. No province-wide road closure or general shutdown of major mines has been established. Indicators \| (1) Status of the abducted civilians; (2) further attacks around Wamba and neighbouring settlements; (3) changes in Congolese–Ugandan security deployments near Mambasa; (4) displacement disrupting local transport or healthcare. Further attacks across additional settlements would materially change the risk picture for dispersed worksites and outsourced transport. Sources \| [Associated Press, 11 Nov 2026](https://apnews.com/article/c1c568db3a670679818aa426cf28fc80); [Le Potentiel, 11 Nov 2026](https://lepotentiel.cd/2026/11/11/ituri-22-civils-tues-dans-des-attaques-attribuees-aux-adf-a-mambasa/); [Radio Elimu, 11 Nov 2026](https://radioelimu.uor.ac/mambasa-les-presumes-adf-attaquent-8-localites-au-moins-22-morts-et-des-degats-materiels/).
